title: Production native DTMF owned SDK, private audience and fault/recovery paths
scope: Isolated local macOS arm64 production Store/service/Core/server and public Rust SDK on signed native QUIC. Each of13 named cases runs EdDSA and ES256. The low-credit peer is a real authenticated negotiated QUIC recipient with fixed4KiB receive credit. Faults act on actual Store or transport boundaries, without replacement IO factories. No named remote/provider profile or remote playback claim.
implementation: All three owned audio types expose send_dtmf through the common owned physical peer. Source IDs come from that peer; the caller retains the original logical ID and explicit optional revision. No automatic newer-revision substitution or additional grant.

Fixed original registration candidates are selected once. Selection and source-observation freezing retry only transient contention during one <=2s preparation window capped by original expiry. No successful batch is reconstructed; no recipient IO starts before durable freezing.

Current Core audience metadata is acquired before current Store readers, with bounded metadata try-lock waiting. The resulting original/current scene fence remains mandatory during IO with sealed native source/target fences and fresh independent named source/receiver permission.

Actual frame reservation uses the same already-signed frame. Temporary reservation contention releases media owners and Store readers before waiting, then reacquires complete current authority. Closed flight admission prevents late execution; all actual IO leases stop before local outcomes are journaled.

Actual HTTP operation status exposes the recorded local summary. Authorized same-owner metadata replay after restart may return the original unknown result; it must not create another job or effect. Captured but unrecorded submission recovers unknown, never replayed as a new delivery.
No production default credential scope, upstream patch, schema version, native writer/transport deadline or test assertion was weakened.

private_journey.scope: Existing real decoded private/public audio and return journey plus bidirectional private DTMF. Explicit named receive grants on retained remote and same-Participant public consultant make their exclusion an actual audience check. After return, completed original replay cannot emit; fresh current signal goes only to restored remote.

cases: Signed raw SDK delivery and exact original replay/conflict behavior; preserved queued events, actual provenance and named receive refusal.
Actual HTTP physical-source refusal and actual HTTP operation.get result projection. Two parsed HTTP payloads, result summaries and signed received frames validate against published schemas.
Owned public-audio source send and receive_signaling while preserving a queued incoming signal across another owned SDK command and completed replay.
Finite-credit pending native write settles unknown with original frame reservation; original replay has no further effect and a fresh signal uses the released control slot.

Source and recipient identity writers cannot overtake a real sustained write guard; current credential revocation waits for sink retirement. Original source work cannot revive, and revoking one recipient does not revoke the other recipient credential.
Cancellation after actual pending IO preserves possible effects and stops later work; no resubmission under uncertainty.

Server restart after actual received submission and injected outcome-storage cutoff preserves record ID, frame ID and unknown. Readonly same-owner replay cannot redeliver, and independently admitted fresh owned source/recipient peers can submit a new signal.
Private bidirectional delivery, public same-Participant Connection exclusion, restored-public fresh delivery and original private completed replay non-publication.

initial_attempts.finding: Source capture reports Dispatch(StorageUnavailable), but handler previously permanently failed forbidden before sealing source/recipients. Capture now reuses exact original metadata candidates and retries only source NotReady/temporary Store errors before accepted freeze, under the original bounded invocation, for <=2s and original expiry. Original request and grants are not widened; downstream queue still retains no invocation readers.

Real signal-credit-4 failure: recipient native policy reached audience helper, which returned Media(NotReady), with touched=false and no reserved frame. Source capture retries already allowed preceding4 actual frames. Current code waits bounded metadata try-locks BEFORE fresh domain readers/owners, then retains the same audience fence through fresh Store read and actual guarded IO.

Recipient selection failed authority-busy before source capture, so no local summary existed. Selection now retries temporary authority/storage contention with an immutable registry snapshot; selection plus source freeze share one <=2s/original-expiry budget. No prepared or attempted delivery is retried.

EdDSA actual credit exhaustion reached OutcomeUnknown/touched=true, original replay did not submit and fresh operation completed. ES256 earlier recipient was refused before frame reservation; reservation try-lock had no retry, now retries same signed frame after dropping readers/owners.

Restart and all positive HTTP/owned/raw tests pass both algorithms. Credit tests partly reached real unknown but one 15ms injection sample missed later slow-target IO. Observer now waits for the same attempted pending child and both source/target readers to remain held25ms, then injects while original200ms IO bound remains.
